projectBackground.name: Supplier Contract Review — Orbital Components
projectBackground.context: A key supplier sent its standard contract. The client wants to sign fast, but several clauses look one-sided.

manager.name: Rachel Osei
manager.note: Plain English: tell the client what the clause means, how bad it can get and what to ask for instead.

assignment.title: Review and redline the supplier contract
assignment.brief: Identify risky clauses, quantify delay damages, handle offer and acceptance and write a negotiating note.

documents.name: Draft Contract
documents.note: Value £500,000; liquidated damages 0.5% per week capped at 10%; unlimited supplier-friendly termination; automatic renewal.

documents.name: Client Instructions
documents.note: Deliveries are time-critical; the client needs a clear exit.

tasks.title: Liquidated Damages
tasks.prompt: The contract value is £500,000. Damages are 0.5% per week of delay, capped at 10%. What is the damages amount for 25 weeks delay (£)?
tasks.tip: Calculate before and after the cap.
tasks.mistake: Ignoring the cap overstates the claim at £62,500.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Red Flag
tasks.prompt: Which clause is most dangerous to the client?
options: Governing law in the client's country
Unlimited liability for the client with a low cap for the supplier
tasks.mistake: Signing one-sided liability can be unlimited loss.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Automatic Renewal
tasks.prompt: The contract auto-renews for 3 years unless cancelled 12 months before. What should you propose?
options: A shorter renewal with notice the client can realistically meet
tasks.reasoning: Auto-renewal traps parties who miss notice.
tasks.mistake: Missed notice dates lock clients in.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Redline Priorities
options: Add a right to terminate for repeated delay
tasks.mistake: Redlining everything dilutes the important points.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Offer and Acceptance
tasks.prompt: The supplier's email 'we accept, subject to a 5% price rise'. Legally this is:
tasks.reasoning: Acceptance must mirror the offer; changes are counter-offers.
tasks.mistake: Treating it as acceptance can create or lose a contract.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Negotiating Note
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence note to the client explaining the key risks and your asks.
tasks.modelAnswer: The draft exposes you to unlimited liability while the supplier's is capped, and it renews automatically for three years. Delay damages are capped at 10% (£50,000), which is low for time-critical deliveries. I recommend asking for mutual liability caps, a termination right for repeated delay and a 90-day renewal notice. Without these changes, I would not advise signing.
tasks.reasoning: A good note explains the risk plainly and ranks the asks.
tasks.mistake: Legal jargon alone doesn't help a client decide.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Notice Nobody Diarised
caseStudy.background: A company missed a 12-month cancellation window and was locked into a further 3 years of an unneeded service costing £210,000.
questions: Why was the clause so costly?
caseStudy.solution: Kestrel introduced a contract register with automated reminders and a standard renewal clause.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Know the dates and the exits.

options: A change to the terms offered

quiz.q: The case study lost money because:

prompts: Which clause would you push hardest on?
How do you explain legal risk simply?
What would make you advise not to sign?
